title: Agent cloud startup Daytona hits $1B valuation backed by FirstMark and a who’s who of angels
slides: Can Daytona's $1B bet on agent cloud hold up?
FirstMark led the round with a roster of angels
Most agent startups still run on rented, fragile sandboxes
Your agent infra choice now carries real vendor risk
Test one production workload before the lock-in sets
thread_text:
1. The $1B question nobody asks

Daytona just raised a billion dollars to build cloud infrastructure for AI agents. But most agent startups today still run on rented, fragile sandboxes that break under load.

2. FirstMark's angel army

FirstMark led the round with a roster of angels who've built and sold infrastructure companies. Their bet isn't on agents—it's on the layer every agent will need to survive production.

3. Your sandbox is a liability

Rented sandboxes weren't designed for autonomous agents that spawn subprocesses and persist state. When one fails, your agent goes dark and your users notice.

4. Lock-in hides in the stack

Choosing an agent infra provider now means betting on their pricing, their uptime, and their roadmap. Switching later costs more than the compute you save today.

5. Test before you commit

Take one production workload and run it on Daytona's free tier this week. If it doesn't survive real traffic, you've learned something before the contract.
